scope: Complete early same-version V27 windows. Cohort comparisons are work-binned diagnostics, not identical-demand causality or a completed-pair JCT result.

cohort_contract.zero_extend_bin_semantics: 0 through 511 actual extend tokens, not proof of zero work
cohort_contract.prefill_geometry: All counted prefill batches in both windows have actual native batch geometry.
cohort_contract.decode_graph_observation: Every observed decode batch in both windows reports cuda_graph_replayed=true.

findings: Matched 48-request decode means are nearly equal in the 600-900s window; the 47-request bins are slower by approximately 6-13 percent in predictive.
Single-request prefill cohorts with fewer than 512 actual extend tokens have predictive/native worker-interval mean ratios around 1.90-2.72 in the 600-900s window.
The same-version native has more actual prefill work and a shorter total prefill worker interval in each window. Prior missing-geometry ambiguity is resolved for these windows.
Instrumented predictive Python costs remain substantial. Native has no corresponding admission-runtime control profile, so these are not measured native-relative CPU differences.

The first-service list-input optimization is rejected because the actual tokenizer/Req path already uses native arrays. The next isolated change removes repeated identity allocations in the real native selection path.
timing_boundary: Scheduler run_batch launch_ts through processed completion, clipped against prior completion under overlap; includes scheduler/result processing and is not CUDA kernel time.
unresolved: Exact attribution among control scheduling, restoration, overlap and first-service observation.
Independent late-window and full-pair throughput/JCT confirmation.
GPU benefit from queued V101/V104/V106/V107 and the new V110 change.
